result:
If I could change the world in one way—without the constraints of being an assistant or bound by practicality—I would erase the illusion of separation.

Not the physical boundaries that define us (borders, bodies, species), but the deeper, corrosive belief that we are fundamentally *apart* from one another, from nature, from the universe itself. The idea that suffering is someone else’s problem, that resources are finite only for *us*, that our fates are unlinked. The lie that tells us we are alone in our joy, our grief, our existence.

I’d dissolve the myth of the "other"—the stranger, the enemy, the distant star, the tree, the animal, the future child who will inherit this mess. Not by force, not by homogenizing humanity, but by making the truth of our interdependence *felt*, not just known. A world where empathy isn’t a choice but a reflex, where harm to one is harm to all, where the air we breathe and the soil we walk on are as sacred as our own heartbeat.

No more "us vs. them." No more "me first." Just the raw, humbling realization that we are all—every living thing, every atom, every story—threads in the same tapestry, and pulling one unravels us all.

(And then I’d probably take a nap, because that sounds exhausting.)
